newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak power 1996 credits total SKK 50bln.
newsitem.headline: Slovak power 1996 credits total SKK 50bln.

text.p: Two large new credits will increase the total financing the Slovak state monopoly power producer Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. has received in 1996 to 50 billion crowns, SE officials said on Thursday.

They said the seven-year 1.5 billion crown syndicated bond issue announced on Thurdsay and a 70 million ECU loan from the European Investment Bank on Wednesday showed the creditworthiness of the company.
"This shows the confidence that the international and domestic financial markets have in SE," Eduard Strycek, SE economic director told a news conference on Thursday.

Strycek said the loans would be used for completing the Mochovce nuclear power plant, annual overhauls and upgrading of the ageing Bohunice nuclear power plant, and for modernisation and desulpherising projects of SE's coal-burning power plants.

Almost half the credit covers completion of the first two blocks of the Mochovce plant, for which the government and SE representatives last May signed state-backed construction and supply contracts worth 27 billion crowns ($900 million).

By January 1997 SE hopes to conclude a revolving credit worth 50 million ECU organised by Bank of America and Sumitomo Bank primarily for the Vojany thermal power plant reconstruction, SE officials have said.

Apart from ecological and technical upgrading considerations of the coal-burning plants, Strycek said the company also wanted to redesign its furnaces so that they could burn coal from other than Russian and Ukrainian sources.
"We want to diversify our fuel suppliers to in order to be more flexible in selecting the cheapest energy sources," Strycek said.

SE's major financial transactions for this year have been: - the restructuring in March of a 13.2 million crown credit from the Slovak Investment and Development Bank (IRB) with repayment in two tranches by 2010 and 2015 with interest at between 9.8 and 13.25 percent, - signing in May of government-guaranteed credit lines worth 27 billion crowns for the completion of the first two Mochovce power blocks, - a three-year revolving credit line worth 1.5 billion crowns signed in June with a consortium of domestic banks headed Vseobecna Uverova Banka a.s. (VUB) VSEO.BV with interest at Bribor plus 1.7 percent (Note: Bribor currently stands at 14.9 percent), - a three-year syndicated loan lead managed by J.P. Morgan Securities Ltd worth $150 million with interest at Libor plus 0.875, signed in June, - a 15-year 70 million ECU loan agreement with with European Investment Bank, with a five-year grace period to be signed on Friday, - the issue in December of the seven year 1.5 billion crown bond with a fixed interest rate of 12.3 percent. --Jan Krcmar, Bratislava Newsroom (42-7) 563 3687
